title: Are you applying what you learned in new games?
lead: Here we compare how often the trained pattern appears in new 10+0 games versus your frozen earlier sample. This is later performance, not proof that training caused the change.
exposureFootnote: We compare how often the pattern appears and how much that rate may have changed. Exposure only shows timing; we do not claim training caused the change.
exposureUnknownNote: We do not know whether these games were played after training.
nextMeasurementHint: A post-training group can start only after the minimum dose; it includes games that started strictly after training was completed.
baselineCutoffHint: Only finished standard games after the cutoff, 10+0.
includedExcludedTitle: What counted and what did not
exclusionFootnote: A timeout, abandon, or early resign is not read as a weakness. Early exclusions follow the frozen Phase 1 rule.
baselinePending: The earlier sample is still being recalculated with the same budget as new games. Until then there is no fair comparison.
sampleLine: Sample: {{transferGames}} new games and {{transferDecisions}} decisions, versus {{baselineGames}} and {{baselineDecisions}} in the earlier sample.
comparisonPending: When analysis is complete, the comparison appears here.
comparabilityFootnote: Descriptive data only; it does not retroactively adjust rates or prove causality.
realGamesNoAlpha: These results do not change exercise mastery.
policyNote: Rule {{policyId}}. Does not teach a new pattern.
examplesLocked: Examples appear after you lock the review. Before that the group stays open and does not become exercises.
examplesEmpty: No confirmed events to show in this group.
futureExercisesSaved: Future exercises saved: {{count}}. They do not enter training automatically.

exposure.mixed_exposure: Mix of before and after training
exposure.exposure_unknown: We do not know whether these games were played after training

insufficient_data.label: Not enough data
insufficient_data.meaning: There are not yet enough games or decisions to compare this pattern with your earlier sample.
insufficient_data.notMeaning: It does not mean you improved or that the pattern stayed the same. It says nothing about cause.

early_signal.label: Early signal
early_signal.meaning: There is a first read, but the sample is still small. The range may shift when more games arrive.
early_signal.notMeaning: This is not confirmed improvement or proof that training worked.

observed_improvement.label: Observed reduction
observed_improvement.meaning: In new games the pattern appears less often than in the earlier sample, and the range is compatible with a real drop. This is later performance.
observed_improvement.notMeaning: It does not prove MoveMirror training caused the change.

no_clear_reduction.label: No clear reduction
no_clear_reduction.meaning: There is enough volume and the range is not clearly below zero. We do not see a clear drop in the pattern.
no_clear_reduction.notMeaning: It does not mean training hurt your play or that exercise work failed.

exclusion.too_few_plies: Game with one to four moves
exclusion.unparseable_pgn: Could not read chess game file (PGN)

return_to_basics.title: Return to basic examples
return_to_basics.explanation: In exercises, misses outweigh verified successes. It helps to return to basic examples of checks, captures, threats, and your opponent’s strongest reply.

propose_next_pattern.title: Consider reviewing the next pattern
propose_next_pattern.explanation: The current lesson already shows better later performance and practice is spaced. Consider reviewing the next pattern in a future review. This version does not teach or replace the lesson.

space_practice.title: Space out practice
space_practice.explanation: The pattern also appears less in new games. That is better later performance, not a change caused by MoveMirror. Spacing this lesson makes sense.

increase_difficulty.title: Increase difficulty
increase_difficulty.explanation: Good exercise results, but the pattern still shows up in real games. Keep the theme and increase difficulty.

continue_cct.title: Keep practicing this lesson
continue_cct.explanation: {{gap}}Keep this lesson and continue with checks, captures, threats, and your opponent’s strongest reply.

pedagogyGap: You are improving in exercises, but new-game data is still thin.

measurement.sufficient_descriptive_volume: Enough games for a descriptive read

narrative.improvingInsufficient: You are improving in exercises, but new-game data is still thin.
narrative.observedReduction: The pattern also appears less in new games.
narrative.strongButPersists: Good exercise results, but the pattern still shows up in real games.

comparabilityWarning: The groups differ in competitive context; interpret the comparison carefully.
dashboardSimpleConclusion: The pattern appeared a bit less in new games, but the difference is still too small to know if there is real improvement.
